item.title: Absolute, relative, and home-relative paths
item.content: An absolute path starts from `/`; a relative path is resolved from the current working directory; `~` is shell-expanded to the user's home directory when used in an appropriate unquoted shell context.
item.explanationMarkdown:
Examples:

```text
/home/rkpatel/project/file.txt   absolute
./file.txt                       relative to current directory
../file.txt                      relative to parent directory
~/project                        shell shorthand based on home directory
```

`~` expansion is performed by the shell; it is not a literal filesystem directory named `~` in normal use.

cards.question: Which statement about shell paths is correct?
options: An absolute path is resolved from the current working directory.
A relative path always begins with `/`.
`~` is normally expanded by the shell to the user's home directory, while a relative path is resolved from the current working directory.
`..` always refers to the user's home directory.
cards.explanation: Absolute paths begin from the filesystem root `/`; relative paths are resolved from the current directory; shell tilde expansion normally maps `~` to the user's home directory.
